batch_note: Yes, at two levels. (1) Twelve of the 24 items (all A/B/C/D-01..03) use one 2x2 dissociation template: two hypotheses, four groups crossing the two factors, and four comparison options. Without fail, one option compares the both-factors group with the neither-factor group (confounded, predicted by both), two options vary only one factor in the direction the target hypothesis predicts, and the key is the crossed comparison (factor-A-only vs factor-B-only) for 'weaken' items, or the single-factor isolation of the target for 'support' items. A student who learns the template can strike the confounded option every time and then pick the crossed pair for 'weaken' items without reading the specifics; B-02 partly breaks this because its key is a both-variables-differ comparison. (2) The quantitative items fall into three repeated shapes: two-condition filter (A-04, B-05, C-05, D-06), threshold ratio with an absolute-magnitude trap (A-05, C-04, D-04), and 'one point breaks the monotone trend' (A-06, B-06, C-06, and D-05 in a two-column variant). In the trend-break shape the key always names the single out-of-order adjacent pair, findable by scanning, and the other options restate the normal trend, which makes those items easier than their placement. Key letters are balanced (6 each), so there is no positional tell.
